title: Pathological Jaw Fractures: Risk Factors, Causes, and Differential Diagnoses - A Retrospective Data Analysis at the Department of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery, University Medical Centre Mainz
summary:
A jawbone can break if it has already been weakened by an illness or a previous procedure. Possible causes include infections, other changes in the bone, or the removal of wisdom teeth. A better understanding of these fractures may help identify people at risk early and improve their care.
The study investigates the causes and personal or treatment-related factors associated with these jaw fractures. It also examines how the fractures were treated, how well they healed, and what problems occurred during treatment.
The study reviews existing records of people who presented with this type of jaw fracture at the University Medical Centre Mainz between 2014 and 2024. These include medical records and X-ray images.
Information collected includes age, sex, existing illnesses, and previous procedures involving the jaw. Fracture treatment and subsequent healing are also examined. The records are analysed without patients’ names. No additional examinations, surveys, or treatments are planned.

interventions.name:
Patients with pathological jaw fractures

Retrospective analysis of existing medical records of patients treated for pathological jaw fractures at the Department of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery, University Medical Centre Mainz, over a ten-year period from 2014 to 2024.

Data collected include

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Inclusion criteria
- Patients who presented with a pathological jaw fracture at the Department of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery, University Medical Centre Mainz, between 2014 and 2024.
- Clinically and/or radiologically confirmed jaw fracture associated with pre-existing pathological weakening of the jawbone or weakening resulting from a previous procedure.
- Availability of medical records permitting assessment of the fracture and its underlying cause.
Exclusion criteria:
Exclusion criteria
- Exclusively traumatic jaw fractures without evidence of pre-existing or procedure-related weakening of the jawbone.
- Unconfirmed suspected jaw fractures.
- Initial presentation for the fracture in question outside the specified study period.
- Missing or insufficient records preventing reliable assessment of the fracture or its classification as pathological.
